date: 2026-09-01

description: "Upload a GeoJSON or a Shapefile and check whether every geometry is valid under the Simple Features model — with the reason for each error and an optional automatic repair you can download. Free, runs entirely in your browser: the file never leaves your computer."
---

Upload a file — `.geojson`, or a shapefile as a single `.zip` or as
`.shp`/`.dbf`/`.shx` selected together — and find out whether every
geometry is valid. If it isn't, the exact reason; if you want, we'll
fix it and you can download the result.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your
browser (Python via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server,
including ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code
never gets the chance to see your data.
:::

Want to see the actual code, understand **why** a geometry can be
invalid, or compare against R's independent implementation? Read the
[full article](/posts/geometry-validity.html).

## Validate

Click Validate to run the check on the current data — your file
uploaded above, or (if nothing's uploaded) a built-in bowtie-polygon
example. No repair yet, just diagnosis: is the geometry valid? If
not, why?

The code itself isn't shown here — it's a fixed, non-editable check
using Shapely/GEOS underneath; see the
[full article](/posts/geometry-validity.html) for the actual code,
editable and explained line by line.

```{.webgeods-python #geometry-diagnose-py}
#| package: geopandas, shapely
import geopandas as gpd
from shapely.geometry import shape, mapping
from shapely.validation import explain_validity

gdf = None
for path in ["/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip"]:
    try:
        gdf = gpd.read_file(path)
        break
    except Exception:
        pass

if gdf is None:
    bowtie = {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[12.45, 41.85], [12.55, 41.95], [12.45, 41.95], [12.55, 41.85], [12.45, 41.85]]]}
    gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame({"name": ["bowtie"]}, geometry=[shape(bowtie)], crs="EPSG:4326")

if "name" not in gdf.columns:
    gdf["name"] = [f"geometry {i+1}" for i in range(len(gdf))]

gdf["valid"] = gdf.geometry.is_valid
gdf["reason"] = gdf.geometry.apply(lambda g: None if g.is_valid else explain_validity(g))

{
    "type": "FeatureCollection",
    "features": [
        {"type": "Feature", "properties": {"name": row["name"], "valid": bool(row["valid"]), "reason": row["reason"]}, "geometry": mapping(row.geometry)}
        for _, row in gdf.iterrows()
    ]
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
```

```{ojs}
// The color is decided by JS, not Python — see geometry-validity.qmd
// for the full explanation of this pattern. Checks BOTH possible keys
// (valid / valid_after) because the paint chosen at diagnosis time
// stays fixed even after Repair replaces the properties.
VALIDITY_PAINT = ({
  "fill-color": [
    "case",
    ["any", ["==", ["get", "valid"], true], ["==", ["get", "valid_after"], true]],
    "#2ea44f",
    "#e05252"
  ],
  "fill-opacity": 0.55
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
```
```{ojs}
validatorTable = sharedMap.tableCell(["geometry-py"], null, Generators, {
  rowClassName: (row) => {
    if (row.valid_after === "false") return "webgeods-row-invalid";
    if (row.valid_before === "false") return "webgeods-row-fixed";
    if (row.valid === "false") return "webgeods-row-invalid";
    return "";
  },
  // Grid.js's default ("No matching records found") reads like a
  // search/filter came up empty — misleading before any check has
  // ever run.
  language: { noRecordsFound: "No results yet" }
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
validationStats = Generators.observe((change) => {
  const isInvalid = (feature) => {
    const p = feature.properties ?? {};
    return "valid_after" in p ? p.valid_after === false : p.valid === false;
  };
  const compute = () => {
    const features = sharedMap.getGeoJSON("geometry-py")?.features ?? [];
    const total = features.length;
    const invalid = features.filter(isInvalid).length;
    change({ total, valid: total - invalid, invalid });
  };
  compute();
  const handler = (e) => {
    if (e.dataType === "source" && e.sourceDataType === "content" && e.sourceId === "geometry-py") {
      compute();
    }
  };
  sharedMap.map.on("sourcedata", handler);
  return () => sharedMap.map.off("sourcedata", handler);
})
```

**Result** — ${validationStats.total} feature, ${validationStats.valid} valid, ${validationStats.invalid} invalid.

## Fix (optional)

`make_valid()` rebuilds the geometry into an equivalent, valid form.
**Requires having run Validate above at least once**: it reuses
exactly the same data just diagnosed, no new reading of the file.

```{.webgeods-python #geometry-repair-py}
from shapely.geometry import mapping
from shapely.validation import make_valid

gdf["valid_before"] = gdf["valid"]
gdf["geometry"] = gdf.geometry.apply(lambda g: make_valid(g) if not g.is_valid else g)
gdf["valid_after"] = gdf.geometry.is_valid

{
    "type": "FeatureCollection",
    "features": [
        {"type": "Feature", "properties": {"name": row["name"], "valid_before": bool(row["valid_before"]), "valid_after": bool(row["valid_after"])}, "geometry": mapping(row.geometry)}
        for _, row in gdf.iterrows()
    ]
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Depends on (reads) validateSucceeded, so this cell — and the button
// it returns — is recreated the moment Validate first succeeds,
// switching from disabled to enabled without a page reload.
fixButton = {
  const button = document.createElement("button");
  button.textContent = "🔧 Fix";
  button.disabled = !validateSucceeded;
  button.title = validateSucceeded ? "" : "Run Validate above first";
  button.onclick = async () => {
    button.disabled = true;
    button.classList.add("webgeods-btn-loading");
    button.textContent = "⌛ Fixing...";
    try {
      await window.WebGeoDS.CodeCell.find("geometry-repair-py").run();
    } finally {
      button.disabled = false;
      button.classList.remove("webgeods-btn-loading");
      button.textContent = "🔧 Fix";
    }
  };
  return button;
}
```

## Download the result

Download the current state — fixed if you ran the section above,
otherwise diagnosed as-is.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Not promoted to shared/ (still only one tool using it): a Blob +
// a temporary <a download> is enough, no library needed. If a second
// tool ends up duplicating this same function, that's the point to
// move it into a shared file, not before.
downloadGeoJSON = (sourceId, filename) => {
  const data = sharedMap.getGeoJSON(sourceId);
  if (!data) return;
  window.WebGeoDS.track?.("download_clicked", { tool: "geojson-shapefile-validator", sourceId });
  const blob = new Blob([JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)], { type: "application/geo+json" });
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const a = document.createElement("a");
  a.href = url;
  a.download = filename;
  a.click();
  URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
downloadButton = {
  const button = document.createElement("button");
  button.textContent = "⬇ Download result";
  button.onclick = () => {
    const base = WebGeoDS.Upload.baseName(uploadedFiles);
    downloadGeoJSON("geometry-py", base ? `${base}-validated.geojson` : "validated-geojson.geojson");
  };
  return button;
}
```

${downloadButton}

<style>
/* geometry-diagnose-py/geometry-repair-py are functional (the CodeCell
   engine still runs them), just not shown: this tool's whole point is
   "same engine, less prose" (see the article link above) — a code
   editor to click "Run" in would contradict that, and the buttons
   above already trigger .run() on these cells programmatically.
   NOT display:none — verified empirically (Playwright, 100%
   reproducible over repeated clean runs) that display:none causes
   window.maplibregl to never become available after all 4 of
   map.js's own load retries, something display:none-on-these-divs
   alone was enough to trigger (removing just this rule made the
   failure disappear every time, 3/3 runs). Root cause not fully
   understood — most likely CodeMirror measuring a zero-size
   container blocks the main thread long enough to break the
   maplibre-gl.js <script> race described in shared/map.js's own
   loadMapLibreScript() comment. height:0 + overflow:hidden hides the
   same content without giving CodeMirror a zero-width box to choke
   on, and doesn't reproduce the failure (3/3 clean runs). */
#geometry-diagnose-py, #geometry-repair-py {
  height: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
}
</style>
